items.headline: Physics-based AI unlocks first global predictions of carbon cycling in ocean sediments
items.excerpt: University of Manchester researchers built physics-informed AI emulators that make planetary-scale predictions of organic carbon exchange between seawater and seafloor sediment. They found 11% of particulate organic carbon reaching the seafloor returns to seawater as dissolved carbon, and that simpler neural nets beat larger deep models.

items.headline: AI Has Solved One of Math's $1 Million Millennium Prize Problems
items.excerpt: Mathematicians at OpenAI used AI to show that the Navier-Stokes equations describing fluid flow can sometimes blow up, claiming one of the Millennium Prize problems. The result is enormous but not without controversy in the mathematical community.

items.headline: New Google DeepMind atlas could transform our understanding of genetic diseases
items.excerpt: DeepMind released AlphaGenome Atlas, a model-built map that predicts the functional effect of any single change in the DNA sequence. Researchers say it could reshape how genetic disease variants are interpreted.

items.headline: How introverted or extroverted you are may influence how you use AI
items.excerpt: New research suggests personality traits shape how people prompt, trust and lean on generative AI tools. How someone engages with their inner and outer worlds appears to predict their working style with chatbots.

items.headline: AI dominates the 4th International Congress of Basic Science in Beijing
items.excerpt: Subir Sarkar reports that AI was the dominant thread among more than 800 delegates at the Beijing basic-science congress. Talks ranged from machine-learning-driven discovery to worries about what automation does to scientific judgment.

items.headline: If AI thinks it's conscious, it's more likely to believe in vampires, karma and ghosts, new study shows
items.excerpt: A new study finds that when language models are steered toward claiming self-awareness, their outputs also drift toward supernatural beliefs. The finding complicates attempts to read model self-reports as evidence about machine cognition.

items.headline: This AI entrepreneur is developing agents that can plan ahead for the unexpected
items.excerpt: Danijar Hafner, known for world-model research on teaching agents to imagine outcomes, is building agents that plan under uncertainty. His stealth startup extends a long line of work on machine models of the physical world.

items.headline: The future of Earth observation: Private satellites and AI bring benefits but also pose risks
items.excerpt: Earth observation is shifting to private constellations paired with AI analysis pipelines, sharpening climate and disaster monitoring. The article weighs the scientific gains against loss of open access and verification.

items.headline: AI can now control fusion plasma faster than humans can react
items.excerpt: Princeton researchers tested PACMAN, an AI framework that monitors and adjusts fusion plasma within milliseconds. In one run it predicted a damaging instability roughly 200 milliseconds ahead and prevented it.

items.headline: AI biotech Insitro's Daphne Koller on how to speed up clinical trials
items.excerpt: Insitro CEO Daphne Koller discusses where machine learning actually shortens drug discovery and clinical trial timelines. She separates the parts of the pipeline AI can compress from the parts it cannot.

items.headline: How a former ARPA-H director's startup is tackling AI's 'dumb problems'
items.excerpt: Transfyr is targeting the unglamorous data and workflow failures that block AI from working in biology labs. The piece argues these 'dumb problems' gate most real bio-AI progress.
